transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-09-30
Start: 16:00 PDT
Duration: ~46 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Ramirez (Redwood SE), Sara Klein (AtlasPay Eng Mgr), Dev Patel (AtlasPay Lead Backend), Liam O'Connor (AtlasPay Product)

Summary:
Weekly POC sync focused on app integration: SDK usage for function/tool calling, structured JSON outputs, and a short results review from last week's inference latency runs. Discussed small SDK bug, next steps for throughput test, and data redaction requirements. Agreed on owners and dates.

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call — Maya from Redwood here, Diego is with me, and from AtlasPay we have Sara, Dev, Liam. Cool?
[00:08] Sara: Yep, hi all.
[00:10] Dev: Hi.
[00:12] Diego: Great. I'll kick off with the integration items we promised last week. We pushed the SDK snippet up to the repo and Maya sent the link in chat, see: https://redwood.ai/docs/sdk (note, demo link).
[00:24] Dev: I saw that. Quick question — in the Node example you show function calls, but our service uses a typed contract and we need strict schema outputs. Is the SDK able to enforce structured output?
[00:36] Diego: Yes, good Q. The SDK supports function/tool calling where you declare a function signature plus a JSON schema for expected output. The runtime will return a structured payload if the model adheres; we also surface a "parsingConfidence" in the response — although remember the model can hallucinate keys occasionally, so we recommend a thin validator on the client side.
[00:54] Liam: When you say "function calling" is that the same as tool-calls we've used with other vendors? Like passing a tool_id and getting back invocation results?
[01:05] Diego: Similar idea — you register tools with the Redwood control plane and the SDK emits tool-call events. For POC you can do local function stubs in the SDK (useful for dev), or wire to our tool service for orchestrated calls.
[01:18] Sara: Our concern is latency. We did a run last week with the hosted config and saw average token latency of ~70ms which was a bit high for our interactive flows. Any tuning tips?
[01:30] Diego: Right. For interactive you want lower sequence lengths and use our low-latency model profiles; also turn on prefix caching for repeated prompts. For the POC we suggest Dedicated-like instance types or use our dedicated pool to remove noisy neighbor effects. We can also tweak batch window to prioritize latency over throughput.
[01:48] Dev: Is that something we can simulate? We don't want to switch to dedicated until we see numbers.
[01:53] Maya: Yep we can simulate reserved capacity with a load test — Diego's ops team will run a 1k-message throughput test on a Dedicated-like config and share the spreadsheet. That's one of the next steps.
[02:05] Liam: Cool. On structured output — our product wants a strict JSON response with keys: {"transaction_id","amount","currency","risk_score"} and nested "meta" fields. Does Redwood's structured-output enforce nested schemas?
[02:20] Diego: Yes, we support JSON schema including nested objects. Note, model returns are best-effort; we recommend post-parse validation. SDK examples include a validate hook that will reject/repair responses if they don't match the schema.
[02:33] Sara: We also need to ensure PII isn't logged — specifically card partials — how does Redwood handle logging and KV cache for private deployments?
[02:43] Maya: Good point. For Private or Dedicated, you can opt-out of persistent KV cache and set token-level redaction. Our Private offering supports customer-managed KMS for encrypting logs at rest, and audit logs can be forwarded to your SIEM. I'll share the SOC2+security doc.
[02:58] Dev: There was a small issue when we tried the SDK yesterday — the function-call payload in the Python sample threw a deserialization error when the model returned null for a field. The SDK should probably handle nulls more gracefully.
[03:12] Diego: Thanks, we saw that in your repro. Diego: (sic) The SDK currently maps null to None in Python but our strict serializer raised. I'll patch the sample to include a null-tolerant schema and add an example guard. Action item for me.
[03:24] Dev: Great. Also, is there an easy way to test tool calls offline? We want to run CI unit tests that mock the model responses.
[03:33] Diego: Yes, the SDK includes a local mock mode — you can register tool stubs and supply canned JSON responses for CI. We'll point you to the test harness in the repo.
[03:41] Liam: On the topic of costs — any rough guidance for per-call cost when using structured output and function calls? We want to estimate monthly spend for 10M messages.
[03:53] Maya: Cost depends on token usage and model profile. Function calls may add a small overhead for the tool metadata. For planning purposes, use our estimate worksheet — I'll send the pricing link; but rough ballpark you'd see a 10-15% uplift for heavy structured outputs due to validation tokens.
[04:10] Sara: Ok understood. One more: our infra requires SSO and RBAC for developer access. How mature is Redwood's SSO?
[04:18] Maya: We support SAML and OIDC, role-based teams, and SCIM provisioning for enterprises. We can enable a trial SSO integration for your test tenant.
[04:26] Dev: Perfect.
[04:29] [04:29] Diego: Quick demo time — I'll paste a short Node example. 
[04:33] Diego: (screen share) ``const result = await redwood.call({ model: 'rwd-large-lowlat', input: prompt, functions: [{ name: 'extract_transaction', schema: {...}}], parseOptions: { strictSchema: true } })`` — then you run result.parsedJson. If parse fails, you get result.parseErrors with suggested fixes.
[04:51] Dev: That parseErrors field is helpful. Can we get sample parseErrors for nested objects?
[04:57] Diego: Yep, we'll include an example in the updated snippet.
[04:59] Liam: Regarding model rollouts — if you pin to a version and we find regressions, do we get automatic fallback?
[05:08] Maya: Redwood's routing supports canary and automatic fallback to a compatible model variant. You can set routing policies in the console. We'll document recommended rollout policies for your POC.
[05:20] Sara: Any concerns with long-term retention? We can't keep PII for more than 30 days.
[05:27] Maya: You can set retention policies per-tenant; for Private deployments you can disable logs entirely. We'll note that in the compliance doc.
[05:36] Dev: One more technical detail — when the model calls a tool we often expect synchronous results (e.g., call to payments-svc). Does Redwood support sync tool invocations in the SDK?
[05:48] Diego: Yes, the SDK supports both sync and async handlers. For low-latency sync we recommend embedding the handler in the same process or a low-latency RPC path. If you need at-least-once semantics for async, we have delivery guarantees in dedicated mode.
[06:02] Sara: We also want to capture failure modes — e.g., if the model returns malformed JSON, do you have telemetry to track parse failure rates?
[06:11] Diego: Console exposes per-route parsing error rates, token breakdowns, and failed tool invocations. That ties into Optimize so you can set alerts when parse failure > X%.
[06:23] Liam: Great. Any blockers on our side to get the structured output integrated this sprint?
[06:29] Dev: Main blocker is sample schemas and CI mocks — we can do the client work once we have updated SDK code and our sample prompts.
[06:36] Maya: So to recap actions: Diego updates SDK samples and adds null-tolerant example; Redwood Ops runs throughput test; AtlasPay provides sample prompts and expected schema; Maya sends security & pricing links.
[06:48] Sara: Sounds good.
[06:50] Dev: One tiny nit — when we tried the live demo the model replaced 'KV cache' with 'key-b cache' in the transcript and that tripped our test TXN ID extraction. Not a huge deal but just FYI, model transcription variance affects downstream parsers.
[07:06] Diego: Noted — we'll make extractor more tolerant and include fuzzy matching in the SDK helper.
[07:12] Liam: Any final questions?
[07:14] Sara: No, thanks.
[07:16] Maya: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with links and the updated SDK.
[07:20] Dev: Thanks.
[07:22] [END]
